actions.body:
Automated reasoning frameworks, such as Popper and Bayesian optimization systems, demonstrate significant efficiency in testing hypotheses and falsifying cyber-physical system specifications. However, these architectures operate strictly within predetermined methodological bounds. They lack the reflexive capacity to evaluate or revise their own foundational epistemic assumptions without external intervention, aligning with insights from ethics-based auditing literature.

Summary
Automated systems can test hypotheses rapidly, but they cannot rewrite their own underlying rules without outside help.
actions.lede: Examining how automated hypothesis testing frameworks operate within fixed parameters and why external governance remains essential.
